strong.text:
Yeon: {strength_line} Strong here just means your {dm_el} gets a lot of backup from your birth date. It's about backing, not about being a better person.

Bom: That backing shows up as a part of you that doesn't bend easily. Once you'd made up your mind about this relationship, holding on or letting go, it took a lot to move you.

Yeon: Which is also why the ending may have hit your pride as hard as your heart. Charts with that much backing don't plan on losing.

Bom: And it's why the checking can feel like work you're doing, not a feeling you're having. Strong charts often turn grief into a task.

Think of the moment you first knew something was off. Write down what you told yourself then. That sentence is your half of the ending.

spring.intro:
Spring birthday. That's tree season, so you got a double shot of yourself: taller, louder, surer. In saju terms, Wood ran the month you were born in. In real life, you've never once waited to be picked.

In a breakup, double Wood doesn't wilt. It keeps growing in the direction it already picked. Great, unless the direction was them.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Double Wood. So the stubbornness is seasonal AND personal. Great.

summer.intro:
You're a tree born in the heat. All that growing goes straight into showing: big plans, big talk, big gestures. Summer burns through a pine fast, so you look unstoppable right up until the plans run out and you go very quiet.

So you grieve in two modes: bright and busy in public, flat on the couch in private. The checking happens on the couch days.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You give off so much light. Just save a little for yourself.

autumn.intro:
Autumn is axe season, and you're the tree. Life started trimming you early: rules, pressure, people with opinions. It made you sharper and more disciplined than other pines. It also made you allergic to being told what to do.

A breakup feels like one more person deciding for you. Checking their page is how you take a little control back. It only feels like it does.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Pruned young. Explains the posture. And the attitude.

winter.intro:
A winter pine. The cold kept you quiet on the outside while the roots drank everything. You think longer than you let on, and when you finally move, it's because you already decided weeks ago.

So you grieve underground. Nobody sees you miss them. You check quietly, decide nothing out loud, and then wonder why it still aches long after.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You look calm. Underneath, you've been planning for weeks.

earth.intro:
Born in the between-season weeks, when soil runs the show. For a tree, that means work: you're always building, fixing, providing. Very useful. Very tired. Somebody should ask what you want for once.

So the breakup became another job: understand it, fix it, file it. Checking their page is you still clocking in on a project that shut down.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Rest is not a prize you win. It's allowed.

why-you-check.heading: Why you still check, the short version
why-you-check.text:
For a Tall Pine, it isn't over until it's fair. Somewhere in their feed you're hoping to find the moment they finally understood your side.

Yeon: A caption that says "I was wrong." A sad song on their story. A small public apology to you, specifically.

Bom: You won't find it there. You keep looking because a tree can't stop growing toward where the light used to be.

That's the first reason, and the one you'd admit to. There are two more you wouldn't.

Yeon: Chapter 4 reads what your answers say about the timing, and why the urge got louder instead of quieter. Chapter 5 takes the whole loop apart and gives you something to do at 1am with the phone already in your hand.

Bom: The second reason is the one that keeps you up. The third is the one that makes you open the app before you've decided to.

<!-- IMG -->

their-side.heading: How it may have looked from their side
their-side.text:
We can't know what they think. But from where they stood, it may have looked like this: the most dependable person around, and still not much of a say for them.

Yeon: Ouch. Possible, though.

Bom: You were building something for the two of you. They may have felt it was built for them, not with them. Both can be true.

Yeon: That's the half you haven't looked at yet. And it's one reason their page pulls: part of you is still waiting for them to say the dependable part out loud.

<!-- IMG -->

open.title: You only plan forward. So why do you keep looking back?
open.text:
You're not someone who looks back. You plan forward. And yet maybe here you are, late at night, scrolling back to an old photo.

Bom: You miss them.

Yeon: You miss being right about where it was going.

You tell yourself it's a quick look. Bet ten minutes later you know whether they kept the job you thought they should take.

Yeon: You built a future with them in it. Now you're standing on the empty lot with a hard hat at midnight.

### The tell you think nobody sees

When someone mentions them, you probably change the subject fast. Then you think about them for the rest of the night. Out loud it's "I hope they're happy." In your head it's closer to a performance review.

Yeon: Maybe you've even checked how far their new place is from their work. On a map.

Bom: That's not nosiness. That's a planner whose plan got canceled, and who hasn't found the next thing to build yet.

Yeon: Which is worth a closer look. Next page.

spring.intro:
Spring birthday for the vine. Everything around you was growing, so you learned to grow toward whatever held still long enough. Charming. Flexible. Absolutely capable of getting your way while people believe they chose it.

So when the thing you grew around leaves, you keep reaching for the shape of it. Their page is the closest thing to the old wall.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Double Wood vine. You don't push. You wrap. Same result.

summer.intro:
A flower in full sun. You bloom in public: the outfit, the story, the laugh across the room. The cost is that you wilt on the inside when nobody's watering you, and you'd rather die than ask.

Heartbreak makes you bloom harder in public. Then you go home, open their page, and check if anyone noticed the bloom.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You're so easy to love. You just don't always let anyone try.

autumn.intro:
Autumn is cutting season, and you're the soft stem. You grew up reading rooms for danger, learning who's sharp and how to bend before they swing. That's why you're so good with people. It's also why you apologize to furniture.

You read rooms for danger, so you read their page the same way. Every new face in their photos gets the full threat assessment.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You flinch at "can we talk" like it's a fire alarm.

winter.intro:
A winter flower. Cold outside, so you grew inward: rich head, private feelings, a whole inner world nobody gets the password to. When you trust someone, it's total. Getting there takes a season.

A winter flower takes a season to let someone in, and a lot longer than that to let them out. Nobody else sees how long.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your inside is so much warmer than you let people see.

earth.intro:
Born in the weeks between seasons, when the soil takes over. For a vine, that means you grow by managing things: schedules, people, plans. You're the reason the group trip happened. Nobody thanked you properly.

So you managed the relationship, and now you're managing the breakup. Checking their page is you still keeping their calendar.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Unpaid project manager of every friendship. Since birth.

why-you-check.heading: Why you still check, the short version
why-you-check.text:
You grew around them, and a vine doesn't stop reaching just because the wall moved. One look feels like holding on without having to say so.

Bom: It's a very quiet kind of holding. Nobody knows you do it. That's the point.

Yeon: Six minutes, every night. Long enough to see everything. Short enough to tell yourself it doesn't count.

That's the first reason. There are two more, and they matter more than the first.

Yeon: Chapter 4 reads what your answers give away about the timing. Chapter 5 takes the whole loop apart and hands you something to do at 1am, before the thumb opens the app.

Bom: One of those two reasons has nothing to do with them at all. It's about who you are when there's no one to wrap around.

<!-- IMG -->

their-side.heading: How it may have looked from their side
their-side.text:
We can't know what they think. From their side, though, it may have looked like this: someone easy to love, kind, up for anything, and very hard to read. "What do they actually want?" may have stayed a question.

Yeon: They may have known your coffee order and never your preferences, because you rarely said them.

Bom: It doesn't mean you didn't matter. It means you may have made yourself hard to find, and people struggle to hold on to someone they can't find.

Yeon: That's the half you haven't looked at. It's also why you check: to see if they're looking for you now.

<!-- IMG -->

open.title: Maybe you didn't just lose them. Maybe you lost the you that fit them.
open.text:
Maybe their favorite show became your favorite show. Maybe their friends became your weekends. Now you're standing in the middle of your own life going "wait, what do I like?"

Bom: You adapt because you love.

Yeon: You adapt so well that nobody, including you, can find you afterward.

So you look at their page to find out. What they're watching, where they went on Saturday, who's in the group photo now. It feels like checking on them. It's closer to checking where your own life went.

Yeon: Missing persons report, filed with the wrong department.

### The tell you think nobody sees

Maybe you still say "we" sometimes. Not out loud, mostly. In your head, ordering food, you still pick the thing they'd want to share.

Bom: That's a vine reaching for the old wall. It's not weakness. It's how you're built to grow.

Yeon: It's also a clue worth following. Next page.

panel.text: Everything grows a little when you're around.

summer.intro:
Rain in summer, gone the moment it lands. You chase what you want in quiet, clever ways, and you vanish when a room gets too loud. People find you fascinating. They also never quite know where you went.

So this one ended quietly too, whoever moved first. Now you visit their page the same way. Quietly, no trace.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You slipped out of the party without saying bye. Again. Iconic.

autumn.intro:
Autumn rain, fed by cool clean air. Intuitive to the point of spooky. You know who's lying, who's sad, and who's about to text before your phone even lights up.

So your gut has opinions about their posts. You decide who the song was about before you finish hearing it.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your gut is right more often than your decisions are.

winter.intro:
Winter rain. Double water. Still, deep, mostly internal. You feel everything at full volume and show about four percent of it. Your notes app has more emotional range than most novels.

So the breakup is happening at full volume inside, and four percent of it is showing. The checking is in the other ninety-six.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your quiet isn't empty. It's full.

earth.intro:
Rain falling on hard ground. Born in the soil weeks, so you met walls early: rules, expectations, people who didn't get you. You learned to soak in slowly instead of crashing through. Patient. Persistent. Underrated.

So you're wearing this breakup down slowly, the way rain does. Checking is the part that keeps the wall wet.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You don't fight walls. You just wear them down. Over years.

why-you-check.heading: Why you still check, the short version
why-you-check.text:
You felt the connection more than anyone could see, and you want to know if they felt it too. Their feed won't tell you. You look anyway.

Bom: You're looking for proof it was real. That it wasn't only in your head.

Yeon: And you're very good at finding proof. You could find proof in a grocery list.

That's the first reason. There are two more, and one of them is why it's worse in the quiet hours.

Yeon: Chapter 4 reads what your answers give away about the timing. Chapter 5 takes the loop apart and gives you something to do at 1am, before you start reading signs into a playlist.

Bom: The other reason is about the words you never said. Checking is easier than saying them.

<!-- IMG -->

their-side.heading: How it may have looked from their side
their-side.text:
We can't know what they think. From their side, though, you may have understood them better than anyone, while they rarely knew what was going on with you until much later.

Yeon: Feelings delivered like old mail.

Bom: You may have read them perfectly and kept yourself unreadable, mostly to stay safe. That leaves the other person no way to meet you halfway.

Yeon: That's the half you haven't looked at. It's also why you look for signs on their page: you're hoping they'll read you the way you read them.

<!-- IMG -->

open.title: Maybe you felt it ending before anyone said a word.
open.text:
Maybe you felt the temperature change. The shorter replies. The way they said your name differently. A Rain can notice long before an ending, and then spend that time pretending not to.

Bom: You were hoping you were wrong.

Yeon: You're rarely wrong about people. That's the annoying part.

Now you read their page the way you read them: for signs. A song lyric, a quote, a blurry photo of the sky. You decide what it means. Sometimes you decide it's about you.

Yeon: It was a sunset, Rain. Sometimes a sunset is just a sunset.

<!-- IMG -->

In saju, a birth date is read through five elements: Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal and Water. Your Day Master is the element of the day you were born, and yours is {dm_el}, the {nick_word}. We use it as a lens for understanding yourself, not as a prediction about anyone.
open.end:
<!-- IMG -->

### The tell you think nobody sees

Maybe there's a message to them in your notes app. A long one, very honest, very beautiful, never sent. Some nights you reread it and change one word.

Yeon: "Always" becomes "often". Big week.

Bom: Rain says everything to the ground and nothing to the sky. You feel all of it and keep almost all of it in.

Yeon: Keeping it in is worth a closer look. Next page.
